## AbstractClick to copy section linkSection link copied!
A UHPLC-(ESI+)-MS/MS method was developed and validated for the simultaneous determination of glucoraphanin (GR), sulforaphane (SF), sulforaphane-glutathione (SF-GSH), sulforaphane-cysteine (SF-CYS), and sulforaphane-N-acetyl-cysteine (SF-NAC), in a range of biological materials (digesta, cell culture medium, cell lysates, urine) with no sample pretreatment. The limit of detection (LODs) ranged from 0.03 to 1.95 μg L
–1. The intra- and interday variation was ≤15% and recoveries were ≥85%. Linearity ranged from 3.90 to 1000 μg L –1 (GR), 0.06–500 μg L –1 (SF), 3.90–1000 μg L –1 (SF-NAC), and 62.5–500 μg L –1 for SF-CYS and SF-GSH.

(22) Franco et al. (2016) developed a LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous measurement of GSLs and its ITCs, however, these methods were only validated in plant materials, not in biological samples. (23) Andini et al. (2020) developed a UHPLC-ESI-MS
nmethod for the simultaneous analysis of a wide range of GSLs and ITCs by derivatizing the ITCs with N-acetyl-l-cysteine (NAC). (24) Ultrahigh pressure liquid chromatography coupled with MS/MS (UHPLC-MS/MS) methods have been used to determine intact GSLs and/or their metabolites in plant extracts and in pharmacokinetics studies.
(19,24,25) However, due to the complicated matrix of biological samples (digestive juices, serum, urine), a solid phase extraction (SPE) precleanup step is generally required for sample analysis. (25,26) Pretreatments are costly and time intensive and can reduce sensitivity. Thus, the current HPLC- and UHPLC-MS/MS methods face limitations in their ability to measure GR, SF, and its metabolites in different biological fluids (e.g., urine and serum) simultaneously without pretreatments.

Overall, our new analytical method can be applied for quantification of GR, SF, and SF metabolites at low concentrations in plants and biological samples.
